title: The Risks of a New U.S. Approach in Ukraine

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带300张你最珍爱的藏品去上班，然后把DJ台变成一个美丽的、有50年历史的活生生的流行快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就去你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼推出的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔维尼斯。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: From the beginning of the war in Ukraine, the United States took pains to avoid the appearance that it was entering a direct confrontation with Russia.
sentences.zh: 从乌克兰战争爆发之初，美国就小心翼翼地避免给人留下它正在与俄罗斯发生直接对抗的印象。

sentences.en: This week, that may have begun to change.
sentences.zh: 本周，这种情况可能开始改变了。

sentences.en: My colleague, David Sanger, on the new U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的同事大卫·桑格将为我们讲述美国的新

sentences.en: approach and the risks it carries.
sentences.zh: 方针及其所带来的风险。

sentences.en: It's Friday, April 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月29日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, David, we've seen a lot of activity by the United States over the past week in regards to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，过去一周我们看到美国在乌克兰问题上有许多动作。

sentences.en: And I want you to walk us through exactly what the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想请你为我们详细梳理一下美国

sentences.en: has been doing.
sentences.zh: 到底做了什么。

sentences.en: Well, Sabrina, the most important thing that happened was seeing senior American officials walking around Kyiv and meeting with President Vladimir Zelensky.
sentences.zh: 好的，萨布丽娜，最重要的事情是看到美国高级官员在基辅四处走访，并会见了弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基总统。

sentences.en: You know, there had been a succession of Europeans who came into Kyiv, including Boris Johnson and a number of other European leaders.
sentences.zh: 你知道，之前有一连串欧洲人访问了基辅，包括鲍里斯·约翰逊和许多其他欧洲领导人。

sentences.en: But the Secret Service would not let President Biden go into an area that the Russians could easily shell.
sentences.zh: 但特勤局不允许拜登总统前往俄罗斯人可以轻易轰炸的地区。

sentences.en: So, they decided that the next best thing to do was to send Secretary of State Antony Lincoln and Lloyd Austin, the Defense Secretary, in together.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们决定退而求其次的做法是，派遣国务卿安东尼·布林肯和国防部长劳埃德·奥斯汀一同前往。

sentences.en: They actually landed a military plane in Poland.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上用军机降落在波兰。

sentences.en: They left their press corps there.
sentences.zh: 他们把新闻团队留在了那里。

sentences.en: They got onto a train where the windows were blackened.
sentences.zh: 他们登上一列窗户被涂黑的火车。

sentences.en: And they had the train take them in to Kyiv with a complete news blackout so that the Russians wouldn't know when they were coming.
sentences.zh: 他们让火车把他们载入基辅，并实行完全的新闻封锁，这样俄罗斯人就不会知道他们什么时候来。

sentences.en: And so, this was the first time that we had actually seen Americans there.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们第一次真正看到美国人出现在那里。

sentences.en: And then they left the country, returned to Poland on a train, and met up with their small press corps.
sentences.zh: 然后他们离开该国，坐火车返回波兰，并与他们的小型新闻团队会合。

sentences.en: This was, in our judgment, an important moment to be there, an important moment for Ukraine, for the war.
sentences.zh: 在我们看来，这是身处那里的一个重要时刻，对乌克兰、对这场战争而言都是一个重要时刻。

sentences.en: And Secretary Blinken and Secretary Austin held a press conference.
sentences.zh: 布林肯国务卿和奥斯汀部长举行了一场记者会。

sentences.en: And that's when things got sort of interesting, Sabrina, because at one moment...
sentences.zh: 正是在那时，事情变得有点有趣了，萨布丽娜，因为在某个时刻……

sentences.en: Are you defining America's goals for success any differently in Ukraine now than you were at the beginning of this war?
sentences.zh: 你们现在对乌克兰取得成功的美国目标定义，是否与这场战争刚开始时有所不同？

sentences.en: And if so, what are those goals today?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，今天这些目标是什么？

sentences.en: Secretary Austin was asked about their objectives.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀部长被问及他们的目标是什么。

sentences.en: And what he said was...
sentences.zh: 而他的回答是……

sentences.en: We want to see Russia weakened to the degree that it can't do the kinds of things that it has done in invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我们希望看到俄罗斯被削弱到这样的程度：它无法再做出像入侵乌克兰那样的事情。

sentences.en: So, David, this sounds pretty serious.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，这听起来相当严重。

sentences.en: I mean, weaken Russia to the point that it can't do what it's done in Ukraine again.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把俄罗斯削弱到它无法再次做出在乌克兰所做之事的程度。

sentences.en: But is this the official White House position?
sentences.zh: 但这真的是白宫的官方立场吗？

sentences.en: Well, it may be.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许是的。

sentences.en: It actually set off a fairly frenzied reaction in the White House.
sentences.zh: 它实际上在白宫引发了一场相当狂热的反应。

sentences.en: They came out and said, don't read too much into what Secretary Austin said.
sentences.zh: 他们出来表示，不要对奥斯汀部长的话作过多解读。

sentences.en: And that's because previously, American officials, they noted, had simply said that they wanted Russia to emerge from the Ukraine conflict in a strategically weakened state.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他们指出，此前美国官员只是表示，他们希望俄罗斯在乌克兰冲突结束后处于一种战略上被削弱的状态。

sentences.en: But no one knows what that means.
sentences.zh: 但没有人知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: I mean, it could be economically weakened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能是经济上被削弱。

sentences.en: It could be their reputation's been sullied.
sentences.zh: 可能是他们的声誉受损。

sentences.en: It could be that no one thinks their military is 10 feet tall anymore after all the mistakes they made.
sentences.zh: 也可能是经历了种种错误之后，再也没有人觉得他们的军队有三头六臂了。

sentences.en: But Austin did something a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯汀做了一点点不同的事情。

sentences.en: By saying the words that the United States wanted to make sure that the Russian military can't do the kinds of things it has done in invading Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 通过说出美国希望确保俄罗斯军队再也无法做出入侵乌克兰时那种事情的话，

sentences.en: he seemed to suggest that the real goal of the United States is to degrade Russian power, and certainly Russian military power, for years to come.
sentences.zh: 他似乎在暗示，美国真正的目标是在未来几年里削弱俄罗斯的力量，当然也包括俄罗斯的军事力量。

sentences.en: Now, presumably, that means at least as long as Vladimir Putin is in office.
sentences.zh: 现在，据推断，这至少意味着只要弗拉基米尔·普京还在任上，就要这么做。

sentences.en: And David, this sounds like a much more aggressive stance toward Russia.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这听起来像是对俄罗斯采取了更具侵略性的立场。

sentences.en: So help me understand that.
sentences.zh: 所以请帮我理解这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, what was the Americans' position at the outset, and how is this different?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国最初的立场是什么，这有何不同？

sentences.en: Well, at the outset of the war, it was more about Ukraine than it was about Russia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在战争之初，这更多是关于乌克兰，而不是关于俄罗斯。

sentences.en: It was about trying to get the Russians to pull their forces back away from the borders.
sentences.zh: 这是为了试图让俄罗斯将他们的军队撤回边界以外。

sentences.en: It was about trying to get the Russians into a negotiation, a diplomatic process, with the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 这是为了试图让俄罗斯与乌克兰人展开谈判，进入外交进程。

sentences.en: It was about trying to impose economic sanctions to increase the pain on the Russians, including export controls that were directed at the Russian military,
sentences.zh: 这是为了试图实施经济制裁以增加俄罗斯人的痛苦，包括针对俄罗斯军队的出口管制，

sentences.en: keeping them from getting microelectronics and so forth that would feed into their weapons production.
sentences.zh: 阻止他们获得微电子等将用于武器生产的物资。

sentences.en: But it wasn't really about degrading Russian power.
sentences.zh: 但它其实并不是为了削弱俄罗斯的力量。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It felt strategic and limited to the war.
sentences.zh: 感觉这很具战略性，且局限于这场战争本身。

sentences.en: It was specific to Ukraine and specific to resolving this dispute.
sentences.zh: 它是针对乌克兰的，也是针对解决这场争端的。

sentences.en: Because remember, President Biden's goal from the beginning was he didn't want to make this about the United States versus Russia.
sentences.zh: 因为记住，拜登总统从一开始的目标就是不想把这变成美国对阵俄罗斯。

sentences.en: He wanted to make this about Ukraine's sovereignty and a violation of international law.
sentences.zh: 他希望把这变成关于乌克兰的主权和对国际法的侵犯。

sentences.en: And then, as the horrors of the invasion became clear, he wanted to make it about the war crimes that he believed Putin had been responsible for.
sentences.zh: 然后，随着入侵的恐怖昭然若揭，他希望将其归咎于他认为普京应负罪责的战争罪行。

sentences.en: But he had not previously talked about constraining Russia itself as a global power.
sentences.zh: 但他此前并未谈到限制俄罗斯作为全球大国本身的地位。

sentences.en: So, David, was there anything that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，除了劳埃德·奥斯汀的声明之外，美国还有做过什么展现出这种更具侵略性立场的举动吗？

sentences.en: did beyond Lloyd Austin's statement that showed this more aggressive stance?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在试图将俄罗斯赶出乌克兰方面确实表现出了更具侵略性的立场。

sentences.en: Well, they certainly showed a more aggressive stance in trying to drive Russia out of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布了一项非常庞大的额外援助计划。

sentences.en: They announced a very large additional aid package.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布40个国家正在组建一个联络小组，将在长期内向乌克兰重新供应军事硬件。

sentences.en: They announced that 40 countries were putting together a contact group that would resupply Ukraine with military hardware over the long run.
sentences.zh: 他们宣布乌克兰将随着时间推移开始使用北约使用的那种武器。

sentences.en: They announced that Ukraine would, over time, begin to use the kinds of weapons that NATO uses.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 因为该联盟已经快用完旧的苏联式和俄罗斯式武器来提供给乌克兰人了，当然，这也是他们多年来一直在接受训练使用的武器。

sentences.en: Because the alliance was running out of old Soviet-style and Russian-style weapons to give to the Ukrainians, which is, of course, what they'd been trained on for many years.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到以比以往任何时候都快得多的速度将这些武器装备送到乌克兰人手中。

sentences.en: And they talked about moving far more quickly than they had ever moved before in placing these armaments in Ukrainian hands.
sentences.zh: 在需要对乌克兰人进行培训的情况下，他们甚至用飞机将一些乌克兰人运出境去接受武器培训，然后再把他们用飞机运回来。

sentences.en: In cases where Ukrainians needed to be trained, they actually flew some Ukrainians out of the country to train them on weapons and then flew them back in.
sentences.zh: 因此，这是一项我认为自二战以来见所未见的努力。

sentences.en: So this is an effort unlike, I think, anything we've seen since World War II.
sentences.zh: 它更类似于罗斯福当年搞的“民主兵工厂”，对吧，当时他试图把武器仓促运给英国人来抵御纳粹德国。

sentences.en: It's more akin to what Roosevelt did with the arsenal of democracy, right, where he was trying to go rush weapons to the British to fend off Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 但这里发生的速度和规模，确实是我们几十年来、甚至从未见过的。

sentences.en: But it's happening here at a pace and on a scale that we really have not seen in decades, if ever.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，为什么美国现在要转向这种对俄罗斯看似更具侵略性的立场？

sentences.en: So, David, why is the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为他们看到了乌克兰取胜的机会。

sentences.en: pivoting to what seems like a much more aggressive stance toward Russia now?
sentences.zh: 你知道，布林肯国务卿曾在某个时刻说过，乌克兰人已经赢了。

sentences.en: I think because they see the chance for Ukrainian victory.
sentences.zh: 他们已经挫败了俄罗斯占领整个国家的最初目标。

sentences.en: You know, Secretary Blinken said at one point, the Ukrainians have already won.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基依然在那里，每晚都在广播中露面，在自拍中出现，你知道的，依然留在首都。

sentences.en: They've defeated the Russians' initial objective of taking over the entire country.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人不得不撤退，俄罗斯人蒙受了巨大的伤亡，他们的将军以很高的比率阵亡，他们失去了“莫斯科”号，

sentences.en: Zelensky's still there and on the radio every night and showing up in selfies and, you know, remains in the capital.
sentences.zh: 也就是他们舰队的旗舰。

sentences.en: That the Russians had to go retreat, that the Russians took huge casualties, that their generals had been killed at a high rate, that they lost the Moskva,
sentences.zh: 所以他们看到了乌克兰人拥有势头的时刻，他们希望保持这种势头。

sentences.en: the flagship of their fleet.
sentences.zh: 但这是一种升级，而升级本身就带有固有的风险。

sentences.en: So they see a moment where the Ukrainians have momentum and they want to keep that momentum going.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，可能出错的事情比平常还要多。

sentences.en: But this is an escalation, and escalations are inherently risky.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And this one's got more than the usual number of things that could go wrong.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报栏目DealBook报道商业与政策。

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，你提到了美国这一新方针的风险。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 给我们剖析一下吧。

sentences.en: So, David, you mentioned the risks of this new American approach.
sentences.zh: 嗯，萨布丽娜，我认为主要有三大风险。

sentences.en: Lay them out for us.
sentences.zh: 首先，你知道，最核心的问题是：这个计划行得通吗？

sentences.en: Well, Sabrina, I think there are three main risks.
sentences.zh: 我们有实现它的工业产能吗？

sentences.en: And the first one is, you know, the fundamental question, is this plan doable?
sentences.zh: 我们能在不削减我们自己的武器库存的情况下做到这一点吗？

sentences.en: Do we have the industrial capacity to do it?
sentences.zh: 目前这还挺容易的，因为美国

sentences.en: Can we do it without diminishing our own stocks of weapons?
sentences.zh: 有很多过时的装备，陆军和其他部门一直很乐意把它移交给乌克兰人，然后去订购更新、更大、更好的装备。

sentences.en: For now, it's been pretty easy because the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们正在逼近这样一个节点：真的没有多少剩余武器了。

sentences.en: has had a lot of outdated gear that the Army and others have been happy to hand off to the Ukrainians and order something newer, bigger, and better.
sentences.zh: 而且，即使你能保持这种补给速度，还有一个问题：你能让你的盟友一直站在你这边吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, we're running up to the point where there really aren't many surplus weapons left.
sentences.zh: 记住，所有人都围绕着保卫乌克兰这个理念团结在了一起。

sentences.en: And then, even if you can keep up this rate of resupply, there's the question of, can you keep your allies on board?
sentences.zh: 这不是一个复杂的案例，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember, everybody unified around the idea of defending Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这是一场无端发起的攻击。

sentences.en: This wasn't a hard case, right?
sentences.zh: 随着我们看到侵犯人权的行为、看到在布查和其他地方的简易处决，情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: It was an unprovoked attack.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在的问题是，如果你的目标实际上更广泛，如果你的目标是试图永久性地挫败俄罗斯的力量，德国人会赞同这一点吗？

sentences.en: It got worse as we saw the human rights violations, as we saw the summary executions in Bukha and other places.
sentences.zh: 德国的许多人出于所有显而易见的原因，一直在避免激怒俄罗斯。

sentences.en: So, the question now is, if your goal is actually broader, if your goal is to try to permanently set back Russian power, will the Germans go along with that?
sentences.zh: 他们需要天然气。

sentences.en: Many in Germany have avoided provoking Russia for all the obvious reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们需要贸易。

sentences.en: They need their gas.
sentences.zh: 他们认为去戳这头熊没有什么好处，特别是在周围还有一个反复无常的弗拉基米尔·普京的情况下。

sentences.en: They need trade.
sentences.zh: 那么，普京对奥斯汀部长关于削弱俄罗斯的言论有何反应吗？

sentences.en: They see no advantage in poking the bear, particularly with an unpredictable Vladimir Putin around.
sentences.zh: 他可能做出了反应，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: So, has Putin reacted at all to Secretary Austin's comments about weakening Russia?
sentences.zh: 我们无法确定，但在周三，俄罗斯通过其能源巨头俄罗斯天然气工业股份公司宣布，他们正在切断对波兰和保加利亚的供应，

sentences.en: He may have, Sabrina.

sentences.en: On Thursday, the drug manufacturer Moderna asked the Food and Drug Administration to authorize its coronavirus vaccine for children under six, making it the first company
sentences.zh: 周四，制药商莫德纳要求食品药品监督管理局批准其新冠疫苗用于六岁以下儿童，成为第一家

sentences.en: to request approval for the country's youngest children.
sentences.zh: 申请批准该国最小年龄段儿童疫苗的公司。

sentences.en: The vaccine would cover
sentences.zh: 该疫苗将覆盖

sentences.en: 18 million children, the only group that is so far not yet eligible for vaccines.
sentences.zh: 1800万名儿童，这是迄今为止唯一尚未获得疫苗接种资格的群体。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sidney Harper and Eric Krupke with help from Jessica Chung and Chelsea Daniel.

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的妙招。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们对光线极度敏感吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏史或食物不耐受吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
